Subject: MidCity Bank � MidCity Bank �-evals setup & next steps

Hi Samir / Erin,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier - good to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the customer-specific evals running on Redwood: 

1) Recommended models to evaluate
- rw-13b-instruct (balanced quality/cost) - good starting point for instruction-following tasks and summaries
- rw-7b-qa-finetuned (faster, lower cost) - try for question-answering and retrieval-augmented workflows
- rw-70b-std (if you want to validate upper-bound quality on a small sample)

2) Benchmarks & prompt sets
- I've uploaded our eval template and few worked examples to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_eval_templates
- For your use case we recommend three prompt buckets: product QA (fact extraction), policy-compliant summarization (short summaries with redaction), and decision-support (ranked suggestions).

3) Dataset format (what we need from your side)
- Preferred: CSV or JSONL with the following columns/keys: id, prompt, expected_output, task_type, metadata (optional).
- For QA: expected_output should include canonical answer and a tolerance field (e.g., exact|fuzzy).
- File size: start with a 1k-5k sample for initial runs; we'll scale after baseline.

4) Scoring criteria and thresholds
- Automated metrics we can compute: exact match (normalized), token-level F1, BLEU (for summaries), and MRR for ranking tasks.
- We'll also run a small human review pass for n=200 items across buckets to catch subtle regressions.
- Suggested pass thresholds to discuss: QA exact match >= 78% (on sample), summary ROUGE-L >= 0.45.

5) Security/transfer options
- We can accept data via a pre-provisioned S3 bucket (preferred), Google Drive link to a restricted folder, or secure SFTP. For sensitive PII, we recommend encrypted S3 and a shared KMS key.

6) Timeline & owners
- Samir/Erin: share 1k sample dataset + list of top 3 evaluation prompts (by 9/3).
- Dev (cc): will provision an eval project in Redwood Console and add MidCity account access.
- Neha (cc): will set up the evaluation template and coordinate human review.
- Target: run initial baseline by 9/10, share dashboard and flagged regressions.

Attachments: midcity-eval-specs.pdf (detailed scoring rubric), midcity-sample-dataset.csv (example format).

Next steps: please reply with preferred transfer mechanism and whether you want us to include rw-70b runs in the first batch or keep it to rw-13b / rw-7b only.

Thanks,

-Marissa

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and very actionable. A couple quick Qs before we pull the sample together: 

- Data sensitivity: the files will include customer account notes and masked account ids. Are there automated PII redaction helpers you recommend before we hand off?
- Budget: rw-70b runs will be expensive. Can you confirm approximate token cost for a 1k-sample RW-70B evaluation vs 13B?

We can do encrypted S3. I will coordinate with our security team and expect to have a small sample (1k rows) by EOD 9/3. If possible, please only run rw-13b and rw-7b for the first pass; we may queue rw-70b for a targeted spot-check later.

Samir

Thanks Samir - good questions. Quick answers below: 

- PII redaction: we offer an automated PII redaction utility in our eval toolkit (it strips/replaces common identifiers and can run locally before upload). If you prefer, you can also send encrypted files to an S3 bucket and we can run redaction inside your VPC for Private deployments.

- Cost: rough token estimates for a single pass across 1k prompts (avg prompt+response ~ 300 tokens): 
  - rw-7b: ~ $120- $180
  - rw-13b: ~ $250- $400
  - rw-70b: ~ $1,800- $2,700
(These are ballpark numbers - we'll export exact token counts in the Redwood Console when the job runs.)

Per your ask, we'll queue rw-13b and rw-7b only for the initial run.

I've attached the detailed eval spec and a sample CSV. For transfer, can you create an encrypted S3 bucket and share the IAM role/ARN? If that's slower, share a Drive link to a restricted folder and we'll grab the CSV.

Dev will:
- create an eval project and grant MidCity read-only access to the results dashboard
- provision an isolated run with prefix caching disabled for fairness

Neha will:
- load the scoring rubric, set automated thresholds, and coordinate the 200-item human pass.

Let me know if you'd like a short SSO/permissions call - happy to loop security.

-Marissa
